product:native-allocator-policy.scope: Builds the native-shadow static and dynamic sysroots (`--allocator-backend native-shadow`) that the product-consuming rows below receive, and runs the unmodified allocator-basic runtime probe, the observability fixture, and the size-class policy probe through static, static-PIE, and dynamic PIE/non-PIE (kernel and direct loader) products against pinned musl's status and transcript: zero size, alignment, calloc overflow, realloc failure and realloc(p, 0), posix_memalign output preservation, errno, threads, fork/atfork, and atexit allocation.

product:mimalloc-startup-errno.scope: On the native-shadow products, a first allocation in the executable preinit callback, allocations in a user constructor and in main, and the application's errno around the allocator's startup callback match pinned musl in static and dynamic link modes.

product:native-worker-lifecycle.scope: Audit-enabled native-shadow static, static-PIE, and dynamic products run the worker-owner lifecycle probe (worker attach, allocation, thread-specific-data destructors, exit, and final-worker process exit) and reproduce the musl transcript with the scalar worker-owner audit.

product:native-allocator-fork.scope: A multithreaded parent with live allocations and concurrent churn forks from the initial thread, a worker, and after a join, forks repeatedly under churn, and runs a single-threaded _Fork, with allocating pthread_atfork handlers, reproducing the musl transcript in every product mode.

product:native-allocator-stress.scope: Unmodified pinned test-stress.c at 1, 2, 4, 8, and 32 workers including large-object mode, and the seeded watchdog-bound soak covering constructors, cleanup/TSD, normal return, pthread_exit, cancellation, remote free, and transfer, through audited native-shadow static-PIE and dynamic PIE products with plateaued audit counts.

product:allocator-override.scope: An application allocator in the executable replacing the complete malloc family or only malloc/free/realloc, and in dynamic modes one taken from an initial DSO, is used by every native-shadow product mode for libc's public allocations, reproducing the musl transcript.

product:c-allocation-interposition.scope: On the native-shadow dynamic product, an executable-defined malloc/realloc/free receives asprintf's caller storage and the passwd lookup's temporary getline allocation, while list I/O keeps its private queue allocation, matching pinned musl.

product:stdio-allocator-interposition.scope: On the native-shadow dynamic product, every FILE allocation and release goes through an executable-defined public allocator in each dynamic entry mode, matching pinned musl.

product:native-allocator-dso.scope: An executable, an initial DSO, and a dlopen plugin allocate, grow, and free each other's blocks, compare malloc-family identities and errno contracts, and keep the plugin's blocks across dlclose, as PIE and non-PIE through the kernel and the direct loader; libc.so binds the malloc family as musl's does.

product:loader-synthetic.scope: All frozen synthetic loader workloads (initial graphs, TLS, relocation, dlopen/dlclose, constructors) run through the native-shadow dynamic product.

product:loader-libc-identity.scope: The native-shadow dynamic product's copied interpreter and libc keep one identity before startup callbacks run.

product:package-corpus-input.scope: Materializes the pinned Alpine APK closure and index the package corpus consumes (primary-checkout copy or exact download).

product:package-corpus.scope: The selected real-program corpus (frozen Alpine package workloads) runs every tier through the native-shadow dynamic product.

consumer:rust-std-lto.scope: The `consumer.rust-std-lto` gate (`scripts/dev-x86_64.sh consumer-rust-std-lto run`) links Rust std, std-dependent, LTO, and unwind fixtures against native-shadow static and dynamic products and passes.

consumer:lua.scope: The `consumer.source-build` Lua lanes (`lua-static-source-build`, `lua-dynamic-source-build`, `lua-source-build-admission`) build and qualify pinned Lua on native-shadow products and pass.

gates.acceptance: The native allocator starts lazily on a first allocation in preinit, constructors, or main, and eagerly through libc startup, without disturbing application errno, in every static and dynamic product mode.

Workers attach before user code and finish after cleanup handlers and TSD destructors on return, pthread_exit, and cancellation; fork and _Fork from any thread preserve the parent and give the child a usable allocator; atfork handlers may allocate.
The libc malloc family keeps musl's C ABI: argument rules, errno results (unchanged on success), realloc/posix_memalign failure preservation, malloc_usable_size, and size-class behavior.

An application-defined allocator (full family or trio, executable or initial DSO) replaces libc's weak public entries, and libc's caller-visible allocations (asprintf, getline in passwd, FILE) go through it while private allocations stay native.
Static, static-PIE, and dynamic PIE/non-PIE products built with the native-shadow backend link and run the allocator probes through the kernel and the direct loader.
Allocations cross the executable, initial DSOs, and dlopen plugins, and the loader's own workloads run on the native-shadow dynamic product.
Rust std, its dependent fixture, LTO, and unwind consumers pass on native-shadow products.
blocked_by: `consumer-rust-std-lto run` qualifies only the accepted-C products from the ordered qualification chain; its `--development-*-sysroot` inputs produce a receipt that cannot pass, so no passing run on native-shadow products exists.

gates.acceptance: Pinned Lua builds and passes its source-build qualification on native-shadow products.
blocked_by: `lua-static-source-build` and `lua-dynamic-source-build` take no product argument and build accepted-C sysroots; neither can select the native-shadow backend.

gates.acceptance: The selected real-program corpus runs every tier on the native-shadow dynamic product.
